title: Modi in Odisha to Inaugurate RBI Data Centre and Cyber Institute
excerpt: The Tier IV facility at Jatni will host mission-critical payment systems, alongside a cybersecurity training institute for the financial sector.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Jatni in Khordha district, near Bhubaneswar, at around 4.45 p.m. on October 25.
  • The greenfield facility covers 18.55 acres at Info Valley-II and houses four data centres for mission-critical payment and settlement systems, certified to the Uptime Institute Tier IV standard.
  • The cybersecurity institute will train RBI and financial-sector staff in areas including quantum computing and artificial intelligence, according to the official programme.
  • Modi's day also includes inaugurating an Arvind Limited garment facility in Varanasi at around 11 a.m. and witnessing the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat at around 1 p.m.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Odisha on October 25 to inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, capping a two-state day that began in Varanasi. The facility marks a major addition to the infrastructure behind India's payment and settlement systems.

The Bhubaneswar programme

According to the scheduled programme reported by IANS via hi INDiA, Modi was scheduled to arrive at Bhubaneswar airport at 4.10 p.m., travel by helicopter to the RBI data centre at Jatni in Khordha district, attend the inauguration from 4.45 p.m. to 5.45 p.m., return to Bhubaneswar airport by road at 5.50 p.m. and depart for New Delhi at 6.35 p.m. Security was tightened along the Jatni-Bhubaneswar airport route for the visit.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=smGWkWTb35c

The greenfield data centre is located at Info Valley-II near Bhubaneswar over 18.55 acres. Former RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das laid the foundation stone for the data centre and the training institute in March 2023.

What the facility does

The Prime Minister's Office release, reported by The Hindu BusinessLine, said the facilities are aimed at strengthening the technological foundations of India's financial system by providing a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing ecosystem for the RBI and the broader financial sector. Four state-of-the-art data centres will host mission-critical payment and settlement systems and other flagship initiatives.

https://x.com/narendramodi/status/2114186514666225982

The facility has been certified to the Uptime Institute Tier IV standard, the highest tier of operational resilience, and is described in the release as among the largest Tier IV-certified facilities in the banking, financial services and insurance sector worldwide. It is expected to improve the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services.

The cybersecurity institute

Alongside the data centre, Modi will inaugurate a Cybersecurity Training Institute intended as a dedicated platform for cybersecurity and enterprise-technology training, research and capability development across the sector. According to the programme details, the institute will focus on technologies relevant to the financial sector including quantum computing and artificial intelligence.

For India's banks and payment firms, the institute addresses a practical gap: payment systems run continuously, and the staff who defend them need training on the same class of infrastructure they protect.

The Varanasi leg

Earlier in the day, at around 11 a.m., Modi was scheduled to inaugurate Arvind Limited's new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi. The release said the facility, focused on modern manufacturing practices, is expected to create employment particularly for women and connect Varanasi-made products with international markets.

At around 1 p.m., he was scheduled to witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat as chief guest. Held under the theme "Wings over Ganges" to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force, the display features Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter Prachand, Su-30MKI and Rafale aircraft, along with transport aircraft and participation from the Navy and Army. The Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team and Sarang Helicopter Display Team were also scheduled to perform.

Why it matters beyond Odisha

Every UPI transfer, card settlement and interbank payment ultimately depends on central bank computing that cannot go down. Placing a Tier IV facility and a sector-wide cybersecurity training institute in Bhubaneswar spreads that critical infrastructure beyond India's traditional financial centres and, as IANS noted, strengthens Odisha's position as a destination for information technology and data infrastructure investment. For NRIs sending remittances home, the benefit is indirect but real: more resilient payment rails behind the transfers they rely on.
